title: BLACKPINK's Lisa Documentary 'Always Lalisa' to Premiere at Toronto Film Festival
excerpt: The feature-length film, directed by Sue Kim and produced by Sony Music Vision, will make its world premiere in TIFF's gala program this September.
body:
BLACKPINK member Lisa is heading to the big screen — as herself. The K-pop superstar's first feature-length solo documentary, Always Lalisa, has been selected for the gala program at the 51st Toronto International Film Festival, where it will make its world premiere during the festival's September 10–20 run, according to Billboard.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=KVfVQLc_mLk

The documentary follows a year in the life of Lalisa Manobal, the 29-year-old Thai-born artist who rose to global fame as a member of one of the best-selling girl groups of all time. It captures the period when Lisa stepped away from BLACKPINK's group activities to forge a solo path — recording her debut album Alter Ego, performing solo at Coachella 2025, and making her acting debut as Mook in Season 3 of HBO's The White Lotus.

Behind the Camera

The film is directed by Sue Kim, whose credentials run deep in the documentary world. Kim helmed A24's The Last of the Sea Women, which premiered at TIFF in 2024, and served as executive producer on Apple TV+'s K-Pop Idols. Her documentary The Speed Cubers was shortlisted for an Academy Award. Kim spent a full year traveling with Lisa to shoot the film.

"Following Lisa on this transformative and thrilling year has been a true honor and a cinematic gift," Kim said, per Hypebeast. "There have been so many moments on her journey that I think will surprise people and give a glimpse into her world that no one's ever seen before."

"This has been such an incredible year and I'm so lucky to have the opportunity to capture these special moments on film and share the experience with my fans."

— Lisa, in a statement via Hypebeast

The project is produced by Sony Music Vision in association with RCA Records, Tremolo Productions, Salt Water Productions, and LLOUD CO. Executive producers include Morgan Neville, Caitrin Rogers, and several executives from RCA Records and Lisa's label LLOUD CO.

A Year of Firsts

The documentary's filming period coincided with a strikingly busy stretch in Lisa's career. Beyond Alter Ego and The White Lotus, she performed at the opening ceremony of the 2026 FIFA World Cup alongside Anitta and Rema, becoming the first K-pop artist to headline such a slot solo. She also launched VIVA LA LISA, a Las Vegas residency at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace — another first for a K-pop act.

The official synopsis, per TIFF, describes Always Lalisa as following "a pivotal year in global superstar Lisa's life, as, for the first time since childhood, she steps away from BLACKPINK for a year of independence. With the clock ticking before her return to the group, Lisa confronts the fear and pressure of launching a solo career, pursuing acting, and building a brand, while yearning to maintain a personal life beyond the spotlight."

K-Pop's Growing Presence at Major Film Festivals

Lisa's TIFF gala slot marks a growing trend of K-pop narratives entering the prestige documentary space. BLACKPINK's own concert film Born Pink screened globally in 2023, and the genre's crossover into film, fashion, and acting has accelerated since. For the millions of BLACKPINK fans across India and South Asia — where the group has a massive following — the documentary offers a rare, intimate look at an artist many have followed since her trainee days.

"Kim spent a full year traveling with Lisa to shoot the film. "Following Lisa on this transformative and thrilling year has been a true honor and a cinematic gift," Kim said, per Hypebeast."

No specific dates have been announced for a theatrical release or streaming rollout, though the TIFF premiere positions the film for awards-season consideration and wider distribution deals. BLACKPINK is also scheduled to embark on their DEADLINE world tour later in 2026, adding another chapter to a year already packed with milestones for Lisa.

What's Next

TIFF runs September 10–20 in Toronto. With Lisa's documentary landing in the gala program — one of the festival's highest-profile slots — expect significant buzz when the lineup is formally confirmed. For now, fans will have to wait: no trailer has been released, and the wider distribution plan remains under wraps.
